cautions: The confidence interval is wide compared with the trend, so the size of the change is uncertain.
ranking.name: Rain and snow (precipitation)
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, rain and snow (precipitation) in the Arctic (north of 66.5N) changed by +0.028 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval +0.006 to +0.049), which is statistically significant (p = 0.01). Over the whole 24.7-year period that is an increase of about 0.068 mm/day.

ranking.name: Water running off the surface
ranking.sentence: From January 2001 to September 2025, water running off the surface in the Arctic (north of 66.5N) shows no statistically significant trend (p = 0.08): the estimate is +0.008 mm/day per decade (95% confidence interval −0.001 to +0.019). This does not mean nothing changed; the data cannot tell a trend this small apart from natural ups and downs.
